newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end steady, focus on new issues.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end steady, focus on new issues.

text.p: Singapore shares ended steady on Thursday in moderately active dealings.
Dealers said profit-taking in Malaysian second-liners was well-absorbed.
"There is a lot of liquidity in the market especially from the retail market," said a dealer with a local brokerage.
Another broker said market sentiment was still firm despite the continuing volatility on Wall Street stocks.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index ended at 2,216.71, off 3.41 points. Total market volume was 341.6 million units with 232 gainers outpacing 155 losers.
Computer maker IPC shares remained suspended even as news that its South Korean had defaulted on a debt repayment. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
"The market does not need such kind of bad news at the moment. But it remains to be seen how it would affect the company," said one dealer.

Newly-listed Jade Technologies continued to climb in active volume and ended at Singapore $1.08, up three cents. Among the gainers were Keppel Corp, City Development and OUB foreign, all which firmed by S$0.30-0.40 each. Losers included Cycle & Carriage and Creative Technologies. -- Doreen Siow (65-8703092)
